title: Put the cord lock back on a duffel bag's bungee: hold its button in, thread the cord
instruction: The black cord lock has come off the end of the duffel bag's white bungee cord. Put it back on: hold its button in, with no more than 2 mm of it standing out, from before the cord's end goes in until the end is through, and thread the end through the lock until at least 4 cm sticks out of the far side. Then let go: the lock resting on the table, gripping the cord by its spring alone, both grippers clear of the lock and the cord.
context: Many duffel bags and backpacks carry a bungee on the outside to strap on a jacket: shock cord through the bag's lash loops, knotted at one end, a spring cord lock on its free end, the squeeze toggle known from hoods. Let the cord all the way out and the lock drops off; putting it back is a two-hand fix: press the button with one hand, thread the end with the other (the Lock Laces fitting guide says the same). Hardest ability: the passage admits the 7.9 mm cord only while the button is held at least 3.5 mm in (5.25 N), 1.75 mm per side only at flush (7 mm, 10.5 N), and the squeeze that opens the loose 8.8 g lock also holds it. The end must pass 13 mm deep and come 40 mm out: pushed in one go, at least 53 mm of cord is free and buckles at 0.9 N or less. Nearest: TK-462BUT holds a collet's release while a pipe moves through it; TK-UC3UAQ passes a cable through a grommet. Here: a bag's bungee, a soft cord, an end state read from the spring.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. The layout is the same in every trial; nothing is hidden. Both arms start at their ready pose. DUFFEL BAG (fixed): a Bungee Top Duffel, 600 x 279 x 241 mm (23.625 x 11 x 9.5 in.), navy, filled, standing on its base with its length along x, x 309 to 909, y -668 to -389 (its far side 18 mm past the table edge), its end panel facing the robot at x 309. A 1 in. (25 mm) webbing lash loop is sewn at the foot of that panel, centred at y -420: it stands 20 mm off the panel and 16 mm high inside. BUNGEE (loose, through the loop): 620 mm of 5/16 in. (7.9 mm) polyester-covered rubber shock cord, white with a black tracer (Tarpsnow TA-UC-SC3125, about 3.1 lb per 100 ft, 46 g/m), 28.5 g, lying straight along y at x 300 on the table, through the loop, 5 mm from the end panel. Its free end, heat-sealed round, no aglet, lies at y 7 pointing to +y; its other end is an overhand knot (24 x 26 x 7.9 mm) at y -613 to -637, too wide for the loop and 180 mm behind it, so the cord slides 180 mm toward the lock at most. Bending stiffness 0.001 N m2: 60 mm held level droops 0.7 mm. Pen rings 5, 23 and 53 mm from the free end, for reading a real trial. CORD LOCK (loose): a Ravenox Extra Large spring cord lock, black Delrin (acetal) with a stainless steel spring. Catalogue size 1.6 x 0.8 x 0.5 in. (41 x 20 x 13 mm with the button out), hole 0.65 x 0.45 in. (16.5 x 11.4 mm), the 11.4 mm along the lock's length. Body 34 x 20 x 13 mm: two 2 mm faces with the catalogue hole, 2 mm top and bottom walls and a closed end, leaving a 9 x 16 mm open end; hole centre 15 mm from the closed end, midway across. Plunger: 28.5 x 16 x 9 mm, filling the open end; its last 7 mm stands out of the body as the button. Its own hole is 11.4 x 13 mm. The spring holds the plunger out with its hole 7 mm off the body's, so the passage is 4.4 mm wide; pressing the button in by q widens it to 4.4 mm + q; flush (7 mm in; the body's end face is the stop) the holes line up: 11.4 x 13 mm through the 13 mm depth. Spring 1.5 N/mm from the free position (10.5 N at flush). Masses at 1.41 g/cm3: body 4.9 g, plunger 3.9 g. Start: lying on one 34 x 13 mm side, button toward +x, hole axis along y, body centre at x 302, y 130, 116 mm in front of the cord's free end. Simulation: the cord is 31 capsules of 20 mm (radius 3.95 mm, 16-sided collider) on bending joints of 0.05 N m/rad, friction 0.6, no stretch, the knot a rigid block on its end; the bag and the loop are fixed boxes; the lock is built from boxes, square edges; the plunger slides on a prismatic joint, 0 to 7 mm, with the spring; friction 0.4. Real build: the named bag, lock and cord. For reading: a steel rule and a caliper.
scoring: Read every step from the cord's centre line (two ends, 31 segment centres), the lock's pose and the plunger's travel. The scoring window is the body hole's outline (11.4 x 16.5 mm), which contains the 11.4 x 13 mm passage, across the lock's 13 mm depth. The cord is through when its centre line crosses the lock's mid-plane inside that window exactly once (a 7.9 mm cord fits only once). Out, for each side: the length of cord, measured along the cord, from where it first reaches that side's face to its end on that side; the cord's out is the smaller of the two sides (the knot's side is always long). In: how far a cord end lying inside the window is from the face it entered by. Released: every point of both grippers' finger zones (pad thickness and width included) is at least 30 mm from the lock and the cord; unreadable arms count as not released. Let go: released on every step of the last 1 s (20 steps). Pressed: at some step while no cord end was 5 mm in and the cord was not through, the plunger was at least 5 mm in (the button at most 2 mm out), and it stays at least 5 mm in on every step from the first step a cord end is 5 mm in until the cord is first through; a wedged cord end pushes it only 3.5 mm in, so every line above 0 needs Pressed, and 0.5 and up need the press held (a press lost leaves 0.25 at most). The score is the highest line that holds: 1.0 (success; the trial ends once it has held 1 s): let go, and on every step of that second, all at once: the cord through with out at least 40 mm; the lock resting on the table (its lowest point within 2 mm of the table top); the plunger held at least 1 mm in from its free position (the button at most 6 mm out; with nothing in the hole it springs back to 7 mm out); no point of the lock or the cord moving more than 2 mm in that second. 0.75: let go, and the cord through with out at least 40 mm. 0.5: let go, and the cord through with out at least 10 mm. 0.25: at some point in the trial a cord end was at least 5 mm in (with the button out the 4.4 mm passage stops the 7.9 mm cord within 3 mm); a held cord or lock earns at most this. 0: anything else. Doing nothing scores 0 (no whole-trial zero). Why the plunger reading is the grip: with both grippers clear only the cord can hold the plunger in, and held 1 mm or more in, the spring presses it with 1.5 N or more, a friction hold 17 times the lock's 0.086 N weight. Real trial: the top video shows the button at most 2 mm out before the 5 mm ring reaches the entry face and for as long as the cord end is in the lock until it is through, until the end is past the lock's middle (Pressed held); the pen rings 5, 23 and 53 mm from the free end (5 mm in; 13 + 10 and 13 + 40 mm along the cord) are read on the side video: the 5 mm ring at or past the entry face for 0.25, the 23 mm ring for 0.5, the 53 mm ring for 0.75 and 1.0; the depth rod of a caliper on the button (6 mm or less out) reads the plunger; the top video shows the grippers 30 mm clear (a 30 mm card) and 1 s still; the side video shows the lock on the table.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz, control 20 Hz. The filled duffel is a rigid box fixed to the table (fabric not simulated; the cord pulls it with under 1 N), its lash loop two rigid 2 mm plates, the knot a rigid block. The spring is a prismatic joint, 1.5 N/mm; the cord is 20 mm capsules, no stretch, so it holds the button 3.5 mm out; square edges. These are our estimates: the lock's walls, plunger, hole position, travel and spring rate, the cord's stiffness, the bungee's size and length, loop and knot.
reset_notes: Press the button and pull the lock off the bungee's free end (the button springs back 7 mm out). Slide the cord back through the bag's loop until its free end lies at y 7 and lay it straight along y at x 300, the knot behind the loop. Lay the lock on a long side with its body centre at x 302, y 130, button toward +x, hole axis along y. Check that the pen rings can be read.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (full 900-step run limit); demo: 1.0 (601 steps)
